chunks: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah narrated from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah who said:

I asked him about a man who gave charity to a close relative; is it suitable for him to take it back? He said, 'No, but if he needs it, let him take it from his relative from what was not given as charity to him.'
ai.seo_question: Can a person take back a gift given to a relative if they previously gave it as charity?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between *hibah* (gift) and *sadaqah* (charity) when given to a close relative (*hamim*), a common scenario in Shia jurisprudence. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) rules that the donor cannot revoke the charitable portion, but may reclaim the remainder if he has a genuine need, highlighting the flexibility within fixed charitable obligations. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on maintaining family ties while ensuring the integrity of dedicated charitable acts.
